text:
incident-bot: Pager -> SEV2: GPU pool allocation failures in gcp-northeast4. autoscaler queue length spiked to ~800. docs/runbooks/gpu-quota-check referenced.

maya (SRE): saw the alert. autoscaler logs show repeated API 403/QUOTA_EXCEEDED when requesting new GPUs. queue backing up, high tail latency.

kevin (eng-runtime): confirmed from runtime side — allocation attempts return: 
```
ERROR: quotaExceeded: The project has insufficient GPU quota in region gcp-northeast4: requested=32, available=0
```
We retried 3x, then fallback to warm-pools but those are exhausted too.

maya (SRE): @tasha can you take primary oncall? I'll coordinate with cloud ops.

tasha (oncall): on it. gathering current customer impact now — are any customers hitting 5xx or 429s?

june (support): seeing a handful of enterprise customers reporting spikes in request queuing and degraded throughput (timeouts ~30–60s). Ticket #CS-33112 opened.

alex (product): impact: reduced throughput for real-time generation routes, some background batch jobs delayed. Customers on Dedicated capacity unaffected.

bob (cloud-ops): I can confirm GCP quota shows 0 GPUs available for N1 GPUs in northeast4. There's a pending quota request from last week that GCP put into review. I'll escalate support case. case: 1234567890.

maya (SRE): mitigation options (quick list):
- reroute new allocations to gcp-us-west2 or aws-us-east1 via smart-routing policy (short-term)
- temporarily lower replica_concurrency to reduce immediate allocation pressure
- evict low-priority warm pools / preemptible pools to free up slots
- enable model-fallback to smaller variant (quantized) for latency-sensitive customers

kevin (eng-runtime): I'm preparing a canary route to gcp-us-west2 now — plan: create a routing policy rule with weight 20% -> us-west2, 80% -> northeast4 (will shift traffic gradually). Command: 
```
POST /routing/policies
{ "name": "emergency-northeast4-reroute", "rules": [ { "region": "gcp-us-west2", "weight": 20 } ] }
```
Will watch token-level errors before shifting more.

tasha (oncall): doing quick runbook checks: runbook/gpu-quota says to run `gcloud compute regions describe gcp-northeast4 --project=redwood-inference` and `gcloud compute quotas list --region=gcp-northeast4`. doing that now.

maya (SRE): also please pause non-critical batch workers that are consuming GPUs in that region. @kevin can you post the k8s labels for low-priority pools so I can run eviction?

kevin (eng-runtime): low-priority pools labeled: `pool=batch-low, priority=low`. Evict command: 
```
kubectl delete pods -l pool=batch-low --namespace=redwood-runtime --grace-period=10
```
Doing a dry-run first.

bob (cloud-ops): escalated to GCP support, marked P2->P1 due to customer impact. They replied acknowledging and asked for quota request ID and usage histogram. Sent both. ETA unknown but they suggested 4–12 hours.

june (support): I'm drafting customer comms: brief note to impacted customers: "We're experiencing regional GPU quota constraints in GCP northeast4 causing increased queuing and degraded throughput for some real-time routes. We're routing traffic to alternate regions and performing mitigations. We'll update in 2 hours or on progress." Thoughts?

alex (product): good — include which routes are affected and suggested workaround (reduce max_tokens or use embeddings batch endpoints where possible).

maya (SRE): status update: reroute rule live at weight 15% -> us-west2. early telemetry: 429s down 12%, queue length down ~10%. Evicted ~8 low-priority pods, freed 4 GPUs (stable). Continuing.

tasha (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall: current plan to incrementally shift to 40% -> us-west2 if quota still failing; continue cloud support escalation; keep customers updated every 2 hours. If queue length > 600 after 30m, escalate to incident-leads.

kevin (eng-runtime): patch queued to runtime to enable fallback-model-per-route (quantized-small) — will hotflip on flagged routes if latency > 2s for 5 consecutive mins.

maya (SRE): summary for postmortem: root cause = exhausted regional GPU quota in gcp-northeast4; contributing factors = high batch churn + delayed quota approval + no automatic cross-region failover. Action items:
- implement automatic cross-region fallback policy (SRE + runtime)
- playbook to proactively evict low-priority warm pools on quota pressure (runbook update)
- request quota increase and track GCP case until approved (cloud-ops)
- improve customer comm cadence + add status page updates (support/product)

incident-bot: Incident channel thread closed for now; tag: unresolved -> monitoring.
